data.name: Muktikanta
data.gender_notes: Muktikanta is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muktikanta is a Sanskrit name which is derived from the word Mukti, meaning liberation. This name is given to a child who is believed to bring freedom, salvation and liberation to those around him. It is a name of great significance in Hinduism, particularly in the mythology surrounding Vishnu and his avatars. The name Muktikanta carries the meaning “Lord of Liberation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Muktikanta usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of liberation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Muktikanta is a name that represents spiritual growth and enlightenment. It signifies the release from the cycle of birth and death and the attainment of moksha or salvation. This name is a powerful reminder of the ultimate goal of human life and inspires one to strive towards spiritual freedom and liberation.
data.etymology: Muktikanta belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Liberation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muktikanta total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Muktikanta was a Jaina monk and the founder of the Terahutta monastic order in the 12th century CE in Karnataka, India. He is known for his teachings on the 'Three Jewels' and the importance of self-realization through meditation.

historical_references.reference: Muktikanta was also a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement in medieval India. He is revered by both Hindu and Jain communities for his teachings on devotion to God and the attainment of spiritual liberation.
